subject: Peregrine: Marketplace onramp & private-offer sequence (MAP + eval timeline)
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lang <sara.lang@peregrine.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Jan 2028 09:08:00 -0800
Subject: Peregrine: Marketplace onramp & private-offer sequence (MAP + eval timeline)

Hi Sara — great to meet you on Friday. Per our conversation, I’m attaching a working MAP that sequences the marketplace private-offer path (AWS) + evaluation checkpoints and procurement milestones so your buying team can align with Procurement and IT. High level: 1) Private Offer accepted by Peregrine in AWS Marketplace, 2) PO issued to Redwood via AWS billing (list invoice-to details in PO), 3) Dedicated evaluation window (2 weeks sandbox access), 4) SOW sign & rollout cadence for pilot to production.

Attached: Peregrine-MAP-v1.xlsx (MAP with dates, owners, blockers) and a draft SOW for pilot. Key asks from your side: procurement contact for PO, legal contact for SOW redlines, and confirmation on whether billing must flow through your internal AWS reseller.

Proposed initial timeline (flexible):
- Jan 10: Confirm procurement/PO contact
- Jan 13–26: 2-week eval in test account (we’ll provide AWS private offer license + sandbox)
- Jan 27–Feb 03: Finalize SOW and DocuSign
- Feb 06: PO issued & private-offer acceptance completed

If that looks reasonable I’ll loop in Finance for billing specifics and our Marketplace ops person to own the private-offer creation.

Thanks — Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
nkhil.sharma@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: Peregrine-MAP-v1.xlsx, SOW_draft_Peregrine.pdf

From: Sara Lang <sara.lang@peregrine.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@peregrine.com, Mark Liu <mark.liu@peregrine.com>
Date: Mon, 09 Jan 2028 11:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine: Marketplace onramp & private-offer sequence (MAP + eval timeline)

Hi Nikhil — thanks for the MAP. A few quick questions from Procurement and IT: 
1) We prefer AWS Marketplace private offers to be billed through our central marketplace account. Can you confirm Redwood supports billing through the buyer-managed AWS account and whether invoices come from AWS or Redwood?
2) For the sandbox eval, will Redwood spin up a short-lived environment in our AWS account or provide access to a Redwood-hosted sandbox? We need to know network/IP ranges for allowlisting.
3) What refund/credit policy do you follow if we fail the eval?

Looping in procurement@peregrine.com — can you confirm the PO template requirements (I attached our standard template) and the procurement timeline from your end?

Best,
Sara Lang
Procurement Manager | Peregrine Retail
Sara.lang@peregrine.com

Attachment: Peregrine-PO-template-v2028.docx

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: procurement@peregrine.com, Sara Lang <sara.lang@peregrine.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Jan 2028 08:42:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: Peregrine: Marketplace onramp & private-offer sequence (MAP + eval timeline)

Hi Sara / Procurement — quick answers and next steps: 
1) Billing flow: Redwood supports two marketplace billing patterns: (A) AWS invoices the buyer and pays Redwood (AWS-managed billing) — recommended for Marketplace private offers; or (B) Redwood invoices Peregrine directly (if you require a vendor invoice). If you want AWS-managed billing, include the purchaser AWS Account ID and check the box on the PO referencing the private-offer SKU. Invoices will come from AWS; account reconciliation information is available in the AWS Billing Console.
2) Sandbox: We can do either. For fastest setup we recommend a Redwood-hosted sandbox with secure access (no customer infra changes). If you prefer resources in your VPC we’ll provide a short runbook and IP ranges for allowlisting (see MAP column "IT reqs" sheet).
3) Eval credits/refund: For a two-week pilot we typically issue a credit equal to the pilot consumption if we miss agreed SLA targets or the environment is not provisioned as promised. Formal credit terms are in the SOW (see attached).

Action items I’ll take now: create AWS private-offer draft with marketplace ops (ETA Jan 12), schedule sandbox access by Jan 13. Laura will own the pilot success criteria and onboarding. Monica will coordinate the SOW redlines with Legal.

PTs: 
- Procurement: please confirm AWS Account ID and PO approver name by Jan 11
- Sara: confirm whether buyer-managed AWS billing is required

Thanks — Nikhil

Attachments referenced: Peregrine-MAP-v1.xlsx

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lang <sara.lang@peregrine.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 17 Jan 2028 10:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Peregrine: Marketplace onramp & private-offer sequence (MAP + eval timeline)

Hi Sara — Laura from Customer Success here. Thanks for the details. A couple of things on the eval and acceptance criteria so we can make the pilot measurable: 
- Success metrics (please confirm): 1) Average latency <= 350ms P95 for 2k-5k daily requests; 2) Inference cost per 1k tokens under $X (we’ll provide expected token profile); 3) Integration tests pass against the sample dataset (we’ll provide test prompts).
- Access: For speed we’ll use Redwood-hosted sandbox access and provide ephemeral credentials + IP allowlist. If you prefer VPC peering we’ll need CIDR and peering window dates by Jan 12.
- Runbooks and rollout: we’ll provide a short onboarding runbook and a weekly checkpoint cadence (Mon/Wed syncs) during the two-week eval.

Deliverables from Redwood: sandbox creds (by Jan 13), success criteria checklist, weekly demo slots.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Attachment: none

Sara
